stem:
Meena's teacher shows the class a piece of granite rock and says it contains the minerals quartz and mica, and that metals like iron and aluminium are obtained from such minerals.

Which statement about rocks, minerals, and metals is correct?

options.text: Rocks, minerals, and metals are different names for the same thing, so they can be used without any limit.
Minerals are made up of rocks, and metals are made up of minerals.
Rocks are made up of minerals, from which metals are extracted, and they must be used responsibly because they form very slowly.
Only rocks used in buildings need to be conserved; minerals used to make metal products do not.

teacher.key_rationale: Rocks are composed of minerals, and metals such as iron and aluminium are extracted from minerals. Since rocks and minerals take thousands to millions of years to form, they must be conserved and used responsibly. A wrongly treats the terms as interchangeable (term substitution), B reverses the rock–mineral relationship (relationship reversal), and D wrongly limits conservation to building stones (scope error).
